text:
If you’re heading onto Lake Champlain, a Lake Wind Advisory is in effect today: north winds run 15 to 25 knots before easing this afternoon, with waves building to 2 to 4 feet. Burlington is already dealing with light rain, and the rest of Sunday stays cloudy with scattered showers and a high near 65. The temperature call is solid, but the rain is less settled, with the models ranging from a few passing showers to a much wetter day. I’d bring the umbrella and keep the jacket handy, even as the wind gradually relaxes.

Tonight stays mostly cloudy with another chance of showers and a low around 52. Monday looks wetter overall, with showers likely, a high near 63, and the forecasters expecting the unsettled pattern to linger. The lake should be much calmer by then, with waves around a foot, but I’d keep boating plans flexible. For today, wait for the wind and waves to ease before venturing out, and plan on a damp, cool afternoon.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - So far, it’s been rather uneventful in our region as we’ve only been on the very outer fringes of the Nor’easter. Tonight will be cloudy north, with scattered showers south. It will be breezy at times with perhaps some gusts to 25 mph, but that’s about it. There is, however, a Lake Wind Advisory in effect for Lake Champlain until early Sunday morning. The wind will be north at 15 to 25 knots with waves 2 to 4 feet. The wind and waves will diminish/subside during the afternoon. Throughout the region, Sunday will be cloudy with scattered showers, mainly south. It will be breezy, but nothing serious as the Nor’easter begins to weaken. Highs will be in the 50s to low 60s. If you plan to attend the Underhill Harvest Market, it’s a good idea to bring an umbrella and a light jacket.
